statements.t: Occupancy, throughput, and related ancillary services were also impacted by evolving tariff and trade policies, and we expect lower import and export volumes to continue to affect throughput at our sites with trade exposure into the fourth quarter of 2026.
Energy costs increased during the third quarter of 2026 across our North American and European operations, which we expect to continue into the fourth quarter of 2026.

While we have limited direct exposure to the Middle East and do not currently expect a material impact on our operations, we continue to monitor the ongoing conflict in the region and its potential effect on global energy and commodity prices.

Acquired properties will be included in the “same warehouse” population if owned or leased by us as of the first business day of the prior calendar year and still owned by us as of the end of the current reporting period, unless the property is under development.

Non-same warehouse revenues decreased $8 million, or 8.0%, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025, including a $24 million decrease from acquisitions and other non-same warehouse sites, primarily due to the impact of the June 2026 fire at our Los Angeles, California warehouse and lower revenues from idled and sold sites, partially offset by a $16 million increase from recently completed greenfield…

Non-same warehouse revenues increased $61 million, or 27.0%, compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025, including approximately $57 million from acquisitions and $45 million from recently completed greenfield and expansion projects, partially offset by a $27 million net decrease from other non-same warehouse sites, primarily due to the impact of the June 2026 fire at our Los Angeles, California…

Non-same warehouse cost of operations increased $54 million, or 34.4%, compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025, including approximately $40 million from acquisitions and $31 million from recently completed greenfield and expansion projects, partially offset by a $10 million net decrease from other non-same warehouse sites, primarily due to the impact of the June 2026 fire at our Los Angeles,…

We expect to utilize the same sources of capital we will rely on to meet our short-term liquidity requirements to also meet our long-term liquidity requirements, which include funding our operating activities, our debt service obligations and stockholder distributions, and our future development and acquisition activities.
Accordingly, we intend to make, but are not contractually bound to make, regular quarterly distributions to stockholders from cash flows from our operating activities.

statements.t: “We expect these pressures to continue into the fourth quarter and have adjusted our guidance accordingly, but we view them as cyclical rather than a change in our trajectory.
We remain confident that as these temporary pressures ease, the underlying strength of our business will become increasingly visible in our results,” concluded Lehmkuhl.
The Company's guidance excludes the impact of unannounced future acquisitions, divestitures or developments.

risks.t: general business and economic conditions
the impact of tariffs and global trade disruptions on us and our customers
the availability of suitable acquisitions and our ability to acquire properties or businesses on favorable terms
our ability to meet budgeted or stabilized returns on our development and expansion projects within expected time frames, or at all
our ability to manage our expanded operations, including expansion into new markets or business lines
our failure to successfully integrate and operate acquired or developed properties or businesses
our ability to renew significant customer contracts
difficulties managing an international business and acquiring or operating properties in foreign jurisdictions and unfamiliar metropolitan areas
the degree and nature of our competition
our failure to generate sufficient cash flows to service our outstanding indebtedness
our ability to access debt and equity capital markets
continued volatility in interest rates
increased power, labor, or construction costs
changes in consumer demand or preferences for products we store in our warehouses
decreased storage rates or increased vacancy rates
labor shortages or our inability to attract and retain talent
changes in, or the failure or inability to comply with, government regulation
risks associated with artificial intelligence
our failure to maintain an effective system of internal control over financial reporting
our failure to maintain our status as a real estate investment trust (“REIT”) for U.S. federal income tax purposes
the impact of any financial, accounting, legal, tax or regulatory issues or litigation that may affect us
